name: Johann Rupert
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1997-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Johann Rupert is chairman of Swiss luxury goods firm Compagnie Financiere Richemont.
The company is best known for the brands Cartier and Montblanc.
It was formed in 1998 through a spinoff of assets owned by Rembrandt Group Limited (now Remgro Limited), which his father Anton formed in the 1940s.
He owns 7% of diversified investment firm Remgro, which he chairs, as well as 26% of Reinet, an investment holding company based in Luxembourg.
Rupert has been a vocal opponent of plans to allow fracking in the Karoo, a region of South Africa where he owns land.
forbes_facts: Rupert was an investor in the Saracens English rugby team and Anthonij Rupert Wines, named after his deceased brother.
Rupert says his biggest regret was not buying half of Gucci when he had the opportunity to do so for just $175 million.

name: Valerie Mars
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Valerie Mars and her three sisters each inherited an estimated 8% stake in candymaker Mars when their father, Forrest Mars Jr., died in 2016.
Her great-grandfather Frank Mars founded the company in 1911.
She began working at Mars in 1992 and today is the company's vice president of corporate development.
Mars also sits on the company's board of directors.
Mars acquired snack company Kellavova in December 2025 for $35.9 billion including debt.

name: Andrei Guryev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Andrei Guryev and his family own almost 50% of PhosAgro, one of the world's largest producers of phosphate-based fertilizers.
He stepped down as deputy chairman of PhosAgro's board in March 2022 after his son was included in the EU sanction list. He was sanctioned later by the U.K. and U.S.
Meanwhile his son, Andrei A. Guryev, stepped down as CEO of PhosAgro around the same time.
A former communist committee leader in Moscow, Guryev got his start as deputy director at Mikhail Khodorkovsky's Menatep Group in 1990.
After Khodorkovsky, his former boss and once Russia's richest person, went to jail, Guryev led a buyout of Menatep subsidiary PhosAgro.
forbes_facts: Guryev owns the Witanhurst estate in U.K., which is the second largest home in London after Buckingham Palace.

name: Michael Federmann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2009-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Federmann is chairman of Federmann Enterprises, a family-owned private holding company with diversified interests.
Through the family holding group, he owns an estimated 27% of Elbit Systems, a $5.5 billion (2022 sales) defense and homeland security tech company.
He also owns an estimated 44% of Dan Hotels, a publicly traded Israeli hotel chain, through his family holding company.
forbes_facts: Federmann is president of the Israel-Germany Chamber of Industry and Commerce and an Honorary Commander of the Order of the British Empire.

name: Richard Uihlein
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Richard Uihlein is the CEO of Uline, one of North America's biggest distributors of shipping, packaging, and industrial supplies.
Headquartered in Pleasant Prairie, Wisconsin, $8.1 billion (est. revenue) Uline sells more than 43,000 products via its 900+ page catalog to businesses nationwide.
Richard (Dick) and his wife Elizabeth (Liz) started Uline in their basement in 1980; it now has 9,000 employees.
Together, the couple has given around $400 million over the years backing conservative candidates in federal races, according to FEC filings, making them one of the top donors in the United States.
The duo shelled out more than $140 million in the 2023-2024 election cycle. Originally Ron DeSantis supporters, they shifted to Trump after the Republican primary.
forbes_facts: Richard is a descendant of the Schlitz Brewing dynasty; his brother Steve is vice president at Uline.
Forbes ranks Uline as one of the top 100 biggest private companies in the U.S.

name: Jim Davis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Jim Davis bought a small Boston shoemaker in 1972 and turned it into $6.5 billion (sales) New Balance Athletics.
Davis is the chairman of New Balance, and his wife Anna, who joined the company in 1977, is the vice chairman.
He and his family own an estimated 95% of the company, which is private.
New Balance is known for its running shoes but also makes footwear, clothing and equipment for baseball, lacrosse, and soccer as well as lifestyle fashion.
He got his start working for his father's restaurants as a "lumper" carrying trays.
At college he studied biology and chemistry, thinking he'd work in medicine, until one of his professors suggested his talent might be in sales.
forbes_facts: In 2015 New Balance moved into a $500 million development in Boston that also houses practice arenas for the Boston Bruins and the Celtics.
Davis was an early investor in fleet electrification company XL Fleet and owns 9% of the company, which went public via a SPAC merger in late 2020.

name: Christoph Boehringer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Christoph Boehringer's fortune stems from Boehringer Ingelheim, the world's largest private pharmaceutical company.
Boehringer Ingelheim traces its roots to 1885, when Albert Boehringer started a small factory with 28 employees, making ingredients for pharmacies, textile merchants and the food industry.
By the time of the founder's death the company had a workforce of 1,500.
Today Boehringer Ingelheim employs 53,000 people and has a presence in 130 markets.
Some of its best-selling drugs include those that treat COPD, anti-coagulation and type 2 diabetes.
Christian along with 14 members of the family own equal parts of the company; all of them are part of the third, fourth or fifth generation.

name: Rocco Basilico
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Rocco Basilico is the stepson of Leonardo Del Vecchio, the late chairman (d. 2022) of EssilorLuxottica, the world's largest eyeglasses firm.
He inherited a 12.5% stake in Del Vecchio's Luxembourg-based holding company Delfin after his death, along with his mother and six siblings.
Besides EssilorLuxottica, Delfin also owns shares in insurer Generali; banks Monte dei Paschi di Siena and UniCredit; and real estate developer Covivio.
Basilico is one of only two Del Vecchio heirs to work at the company; he is EssilorLuxottica's chief wearables officer and head of luxury brands.

name: Cho Tak Wong
forbes_bio: Cho Tak Wong is the founder of Fuyao Glass Industry Group, one of Asia's largest manufacturers of auto glass that counts Audi, Fiat and Ford among its customers.
He stepped down as chairman in October 2025, citing reasons including the need to sustainably develop the company's governance structure.
His son, Tso Fai, is the new chairman.
Cho is also known for his philanthropic causes. His Heren Charitable Foundation pledged in 2021 $1.6 billion to build the Fuyao University of Science and Technology in China.
The university welcomed its first cohort of 50 undergraduate students in the fall of 2025.
forbes_facts: Cho's hobbies include golfing and collecting art.

name: Edward Stack
sec_insider_companies: DICK'S SPORTING GOODS, INC. (DKS) - Executive Chairman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Ed Stack is the executive chairman and largest individual shareholder of Dick's Sporting Goods.
His father, Dick Stack, founded the retailer in 1948 with a $300 loan from his grandmother.
Ed and his siblings bought the company from their father in 1984, when it only had two stores in upstate New York.
When his father retired that same year, Ed took over as CEO, taking Dick's public in 2002 and stepping down as CEO in 2021.
In 2025, the company acquired Foot Locker in a cash-and-stock deal worth $2.5 billion.
Dick's Sporting Goods now generates more than $17 billion in annual sales.
forbes_facts: In 2019, Stack announced that Dick's Sporting Goods had eliminated the hunting category, including firearms, from 125 stores.
